requirements: The tractor must be unladen, in normal running order, with tanks for fuel, coolant, and lubricants fully filled. Tyre inflation pressures must be adjusted to the manufacturer's recommended specifications for normal road work.

Determines the horizontal distance (x) of the center of gravity from the rear axle center line using the horizontal weighing method:
x = (R_f * L) / W
where R_f = front axle reaction weight on the weighbridge (horizontal), L = tractor wheelbase, and W = total tractor unladen weight.

Determines the lateral distance (y) of the center of gravity from the longitudinal median plane of the tractor:
y = [(W_l - W_r) * t] / (2 * W)
where W_l = left-wheel reaction weight, W_r = right-wheel reaction weight, and t = track width of the measured axle.

Determines the height of the center of gravity above the ground (h) using the suspension and ground reaction method. This requires tilting the tractor by lifting one axle (typically the front axle) and measuring the change in wheel reaction weights on the weighbridge.

Mandates that during the axle-lift tilting procedure, the tractor must be raised to an angle (theta) between 20° and 25° to the horizontal. If a 20° lift is impractical or unsafe, a smaller angle is permitted, but it must not be less than 15°.

The calculation of center of gravity height from the ground must incorporate and correct for the static loaded radius of the rear tires (the height of the rear axle center line from the horizontal ground surface, r_stat).

For specialized agricultural machinery (such as straddle tractors with raised chassis), when the ratio of the center of gravity height to the average minimum track width of the axles exceeds 0.90, the maximum design speed is restricted to 30 km/h.

TDF (Percent) = IDF (Percent) + SDF (Percent)

Loss = Rodent Population * Mean Daily Food Consumption * Waste and Contamination Factor * Storage Period.

Under Amendment No. 1 (August 2021), a previous note requesting members to suggest a minimum volumetric efficiency for roller vane pumps is deleted, confirming the standard's performance boundaries [1].

Amendment No. 1 (August 2021) inserts a precise mathematical formula to calculate the pump's power requirement: Power Required (P_req) = (rho * g * q * h) / 1000 kW, where rho is density of fluid (kg/m3), g is gravity (9.81 m/s2), q is discharge (m3/s), and h is differential head (m); or simply Power Required (P_req) = p * q [1].

All components in contact with agricultural spraying chemicals (such as pump cylinders, pistons, manifolds, suction chambers, and valves) must be constructed from corrosion-resistant materials (such as brass, stainless steel, or engineering polymers) to prevent chemical degradation.

Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and distilled water conforming to IS 1070 must be employed in all analytical tests. Pure chemicals must not contain impurities that affect the results of analysis.

Isoproturon is hydrolysed using potassium hydroxide in aqueous diethylene glycol (1 : 1 by volume). Dimethylamine, the volatile product of hydrolysis, is distilled off and absorbed in standard hydrochloric acid. From the quantity of acid consumed by dimethylamine, the percentage of isoproturon present in the original sample is computed.
Requires a high-precision, all-glass distillation assembly of a suitable type as illustrated in Fig. 1.

The estimation procedure mandates five specific chemical reagents: a) 0.2 N Hydrochloric Acid Solution; b) 0.2 N Sodium Hydroxide Solution; c) 35 percent aqueous Potassium Hydroxide Solution; d) Diethylene Glycol; and e) Silicon Defoamer.

Accurately weighs 1.0 g ± 0.1 g of the isoproturon, technical sample and transfers it to the reaction flask. Adds 50 ml of diethylene glycol, one or two boiling chips, and 1 ml of silicon defoamer to check foaming. In a receiver beaker, 50 ml of hydrochloric acid (0.2 N) is taken, in which the delivery tube end dips. Adds 50 ml of potassium hydroxide (35 percent) solution to the flask through a dropping funnel, closes the stop-cock, and heats the contents to boiling.

Distillation is continued for up to approximately 24 hours. The distillation can be stopped when the contents of the flask turn orange-brown, confirming the distillate has ceased to be alkaline. This neutral endpoint must be verified using multi-range pH paper, indicating a pH of exactly 7.

Requires back-titrating the excess hydrochloric acid in the receiver beaker against 0.2 N sodium hydroxide to calculate active isoproturon content via: Isoproturon (Percent) = [(V1 * N1) - (V2 * N2)] * 20.6 / M, where V1 = volume of HCl originally taken, N1 = normality of HCl, V2 = volume of NaOH consumed, N2 = normality of NaOH, and M = mass in g of the sample.

Mandates that all food handlers undergo periodic medical examinations to certify they do not suffer from skin infections, open cuts, discharging wounds, tuberculosis, cholera, or any other communicable/foodborne diseases.

Separate, leak-proof, covered trash bins must be provided on or near the vending cart to collect wet (biodegradable) and dry (non-biodegradable) waste. Waste must be disposed of daily in designated municipal garbage bins, keeping the vending site clean and free of litter.

Manufacturers are encouraged to apply for the prestigious BIS 'Standard Mark' (ISI Mark) to print on product containers as a certified assurance of quality. requirements: Temephos emulsifiable concentrate shall consist of temephos technical dissolved in suitable solvents with emulsifiers, forming a clear, homogeneous liquid, free from sediment and suspended matter.

The actual temephos content of the formulation (commonly commercialized in strengths like 50 percent EC) shall be calculated to the second decimal place and then rounded off to the first decimal place before applying the permitted tolerances of the nominal value.

When determined by the method prescribed in Clause 13.5 of IS 6940, free acidity (calculated as H2SO4) of the emulsifiable concentrate shall not exceed 0.5 percent by mass to prevent formulation decomposition and packaging corrosion.

Requires passing the cold test. The concentrate must remain homogeneous without any crystallization, solid separation, or liquid-phase division when maintained at cold temperatures (typically 0°C or 10°C), ensuring performance stability in cold weather.

The material must form a stable emulsion upon dilution with standard hard water. Minimal creaming, oil separation, or sediment accumulation must be achieved after standing, guaranteeing uniform field application.

The material must be packed in clean, dry containers made of mild steel, tin plate, or aluminium. To prevent corrosion or chemical reactions, mild steel or tin plate containers must be suitably and properly internally lacquered.

Each container must legibly and indelibly bear: the name of the product, manufacturer's name and address, batch number, date of manufacture, date of expiry, net volume, nominal temephos content (percent m/m), and standard cautionary warnings in strict accordance with the Insecticides Act, 1968.

Any observed or calculated test or analysis value expressing active ingredient content, moisture, acidity, or physical properties must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be identical to the specified value in the standard.

requirements: Mandates that the temephos content shall be a minimum of 90.0 percent by mass, determined by High Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC) equipped with a UV-VIS detector.
Restricts moisture content to a maximum of 0.2 percent by mass, determined in accordance with the method prescribed in Clause 4.1.
Restricts free acidity (calculated as H2SO4) to a maximum of 0.3 percent by mass, determined in accordance with the method prescribed in Clause 11.3.2.

Technical temephos must be securely packed in containers satisfying the general requirements of IS 8190 (Part 2) for liquid technical pesticides.

Each container must legibly and indelibly bear: the name of the material, manufacturer's name and address, batch number, date of manufacture, date of expiry, net quantity, nominal temephos content (percent m/m), and standard cautionary notices worded in accordance with the Insecticides Act, 1968.

Requires weighing exactly 0.033 3 g of reference standard temephos of known purity into a 50 ml volumetric flask, adding 5 ml of internal standard solution, and making up to the mark with mobile phase.

Requires weighing a sample quantity equivalent to contain 0.033 3 g of temephos into a 50 ml volumetric flask, adding 5 ml of internal standard solution, making up to the mark with mobile phase, and shaking well to homogenize.

Injects a 10 µl aliquot. Computes the percentage of temephos content by mass using peak areas of temephos and the internal standard:
Temephos content, % by mass = (M1 * A2 * A3 * P) / (M2 * A1 * A4)
where M1 is mass of reference standard (g), M2 is mass of sample (g), A1 & A2 are peak areas of temephos in standard & sample, A3 & A4 are peak areas of internal standard in standard & sample, and P is standard purity.

Any observed or calculated test or analysis value expressing purity, moisture, acidity, or insolubles must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be identical to the specified value in the standard.
